Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia
Bench: G. S. Ahluwalia
Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Ind:26698

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia

On The 12th Of September, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 6523 of 2015
 Ashok
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Vijay Kumar Asudani- Advocate for the applicant through
 video conferencing.
 Shri Amit Bhatia- Government Advocate for the respondent/State.
 Order

This application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashment of FIR in Crime No.
261/2015, registered at Police Station Tejaji Nagar, Indore for offence under Sections 420, 467, 468,
406, 471/34 of IPC.

2. This application for quashing of FIR has been made on the ground that the applicant was not the Director of the Company when the offence was committed and there is no allegations against the applicant in the complaint lodged by the complainant.

3. The facts necessary for disposal of the present application in short are that the complainant Mukesh Kumar Jagwani filed an application under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. alleging that Santosh Devcon Private Limited is the registered Company and for the last two years, it is being run from the house.

Santosh Devcon Private Limited Company had purchased Survey Nos. 240/3/2, 240/6/2,
240/2/2, 240/3/1, 240/1/1, 240/4, 240/5, 240/6/1, 240/2/1/1, 240/1/2, 240/2/1/2, total area 10.462 hectares for developing a Colony in the name of Mahalaxmi Dham and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26698 the Director namely Sunil Mandwani started alienated the plots at the rate of Rs.1300/- per sq.ft.

The complainant entered into an agreement to purchase Plot No. P-18, admeasuring 40 x 80 sq.ft. at the rate of Rs.1300/- per sq.ft. and an agreement was also executed which was taken back by the Co- accused Sunil Mandwani by taking the complainant into confidence that the same is required for showing to the Town and Country Planning Office.

sentences.text: Whatever amount was received by Co-accused Sunil Mandwani he used to mention in a small diary.

The said diary was given to the complainant and referred the amount of Rs. 7,00,000/- as Rs.700/-
and an amount of Rs.4,00,000/- as Rs.400/- and accordingly a total amount of Rs.11,00,000/-
which were received by Sunil Mandwani was mentioned as Rs.1100/- in the diary.
The said entry was got signed from the authorized office employee of the Company.

The second instalment of Rs.9,00,000/- was also paid by the complainant which was mentioned as Rs.900/- in the diary and thus it was alleged that the Co-accused Sunil Mandwani has already received Rs.20,00,000/- but thereafter he is neither returning the amount nor he is giving the plot and by forging the signature even the Directors have been changed and now the applicant has been inducted as a Director.
It is submitted that although the complainant had given an adequate material to the police but they are not registering the offence.
Not only the complainant was cheated but 89 other plot holders were also cheated.

It was further mentioned in the complaint that after inducting the applicant as a Director, the lands have been alienated by the accused person to different persons without information, knowledge and consent of the plot owners who had already paid money to the Sunil Mandwani.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26698 4.

The trial Magistrate by order dated 18.06.2015 allowed the application filed under Section 156(3)
of Cr.P.C.
5.

It is submitted by counsel for applicant that according to the complaint, the money was paid by the complainant to the Co-accused Sunil Mandwani on 31.03.2011, 23.04.2011, 09.02.2015,
21.03.2015 and 22.03.2015; whereas, the applicant was inducted as a Director on 16.12.2024 and,
therefore, the applicant was not the Director of the Company on the day when the offence was committed for the first time.

To buttress his contention, the counsel for applicant has also relied upon the judgments passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi Vs.
Ram Kishan Rohtagi and Others, reported in (1983) 1 SCC 1 and in the case of State of Haryana and Others Vs. Bhajan Lal and Others, reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335.
6.

sentences.text: Per contra, the application is opposed by counsel for State.

It is submitted that after selling the plots in question to various persons and after taking money not only the applicant was also inducted as Director but thereafter the said plots were sold to other persons thereby defrauding the persons who had previously purchased the plots by making payment of money to the applicant as well as Co-Directors.

7. Considered the submissions made by counsel for parties.
8.
It is true that there is no stay in the matter but on account of stay in the connected matter, the investigation could not start.

It is true that certain amount was paid to the Director Sunil Mandwani and at that time the applicant was not the Director but later on the plots for whom the money was already taken by Sunil Mandwani were alienated to other persons after induction of the applicant as a Director.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26698 9.

Since, the plots which were already sold by the Company were sold to other persons without returning the money to the earlier purchaser, therefore, said act would certainly amount to an Ashok vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17324369/
2 offence.

sentences.text: Accordingly, it cannot be said that no offence was committed after the applicant was inducted in the Company as a Director.
10. Accordingly, no case is made out warranting interference.
11. The application fails and is hereby dismissed.
